sources.entry: Pagure - Lightweight, powerful, and flexible git-centric forge with features laying the foundation for federated and decentralized development. (Demo) GPL-2.0 Docker/Python/deb

summary.name: Pagure
summary.one_liner: Pagure is a git-centered forge written in Python (using pygit2) that provides project hosting, issue tracking, and pull requests.
use_cases: Hosting a git project with documentation and issue tracking
Accepting contributions via forks and pull requests
Setting up a local Pagure development environment
summary.what_it_does: Pagure is a git-centered forge built in Python on pygit2. It lets a project host its code and documentation, take bug reports and feature requests through a ticketing system, and build contributor communities by letting users fork projects and submit pull requests. The page also documents developer setup using Docker Compose, Vagrant, or a manual install, including running the test suite via tox, pytest, or podman containers. The project is licensed GPL-2.0 according to the awesome-selfhosted listing.
notable: Git-centered forge with issue tracking, forks, and pull requests
Multiple dev setup options: Docker Compose, Vagrant, or manual install
Test suite runnable via tox, pytest, or podman containers
Name comes from French word for hermit crabs (Paguroidea)
caveats: The pagure.io hosted instance was sunset in 2026; this page is a read-only static archive
Project has moved to the Fedora forge at forge.fedoraproject.org/apps/pagure
Setup docs reference old dependency versions (e.g., pygit2 0.26, libgit2 0.26) and RHEL/EPEL 7 notes that may be outdated
